findings.text: `source < existing_source` compares `ParameterSource` members. That is a plain `Enum` with no ordering, so the comparison raises `TypeError`. It runs whenever a second parameter targets a slot that already has a source, for example two options sharing a name in a feature-switch group.

`same_source` now lets the later parameter overwrite the earlier one. Previously the first writer kept the slot unless its value was UNSET. With `--upper/--lower` sharing a name, both are given on the command line (or both fall back to DEFAULT), and the later-processed option silently replaces the earlier value. The only exception is the explicit-default tie-break. This changes existing behaviour.

The parameter source is now set only for winning parameters, and only when no source exists yet. If a parameter loses, its own source is dropped. With `expose_value=False`, the source is written but `_param_default_explicit` is not, so the later tie-break uses stale data.

1.reason: Letting a later parameter with the same source overwrite the slot is a deliberate part of the new arbitration: when both options are on the command line, the last one given wins, which was click's long-standing behaviour, and the explicit-default tie-break covers the case where both fall back to DEFAULT.
